title: Grandpa’s Recipe
author: Tadoku Note (original)
summary: 亡くなった祖父の得意料理だったカレー。リナはレシピを探しますが、どこにも書いてありません。家族の記憶をたどる物語。

source.note: Original text written for this app.

paragraphs: Every Sunday, for as long as Rina could remember, her grandfather made curry. It was not like the curry in restaurants. It was a little sweet, a little spicy, and it had something special in it. Nobody knew what. When Rina asked, Grandpa only smiled and said, “Love. And a secret.”
Last winter, Grandpa died. He was eighty-seven. The house was very quiet after that. On Sundays, nobody cooked curry.
In spring, Rina’s grandmother was going to have her eightieth birthday. “What do you want for your birthday, Grandma?” Rina asked.
Her grandmother thought for a moment. “I would like to eat his curry one more time,” she said. “But that is impossible. He never wrote it down.”
Rina was seventeen. She was not a good cook. But she decided to try.
First, she looked in the kitchen. She looked in every drawer and every notebook. She found old shopping lists, a bus ticket from 1979 and a photo of Grandpa as a young man. But there was no recipe.
Next, she called her uncle Ken. “Do you remember Grandpa’s curry?”
“Of course,” he said. “He always used two kinds of curry roux. One hot, one mild. And he cooked the onions for a very long time, until they were brown. At least one hour.”
Rina wrote it down. Then she called her aunt Yuki. “I remember he used apples,” said Aunt Yuki. “He grated them. And honey. Just a little.”

Rina wrote that down too. Then she asked her mother. Her mother laughed. “Your grandfather always sent me to the shop for milk before he cooked. I think he put milk in it. Or maybe he just liked milk in his coffee.”

On Saturday, Rina tried to make the curry. She cooked the onions for one hour. Her eyes cried the whole time. She added meat, carrots and potatoes. She added grated apple, a little honey and two kinds of roux. She added a little milk.
She tasted it. It was good. But it was not Grandpa’s curry. Something was missing.
She sat down at the kitchen table. She felt sad. Then her little brother, Taku, came in. He was ten. He smelled the curry. “This smells like Grandpa’s,” he said. “But where is the chocolate?”
Rina looked at him. “Chocolate?”
“Yes,” said Taku. “Grandpa always gave me one piece of chocolate when he cooked. And he put one piece in the curry. He said, ‘Don’t tell anybody. It’s our secret.’”
Rina laughed. She found a bar of dark chocolate and put one small piece in the curry. She tasted it again. She closed her eyes. It was Grandpa’s curry.

The next day was Grandma’s birthday. The whole family came. Rina brought out the big pot and served the curry. Her grandmother took one spoonful. She did not say anything. Then a tear ran down her face, and she smiled.
“It’s him,” she said. “How did you do it?”
“Everybody had one piece of the recipe,” said Rina. “Uncle Ken, Aunt Yuki, Mom and Taku. Grandpa gave a little of his secret to each of us.”
That night, Rina finally wrote the recipe down in a notebook. At the bottom, she added one more thing: “Love. And a secret.”
